ops.title: cc-context: apply exec.Cmd.WaitDelay to RunCLIExitCodeDir
ops.description:
`internal/cli/lane.go`'s `gtReachable` caps `gt auth --no-interactive` with a 5s `context.WithTimeout`, but that cap binds gt itself, not its descendants: the deadline kills gt, and any grandchild it forked still holds the inherited stdout pipe, so the read blocks until that pipe closes. A forking `gt` could therefore outlast the deadline — turning an intended 5s probe into an indefinite hang.

`exec.Cmd.WaitDelay` (Go 1.20+) makes the deadline absolute by force-closing the inherited pipes a set duration after the process is killed. It is a one-line addition, and the natural home is `render.RunCLIExitCodeDir` in `internal/render/render.go`.

**Deferred deliberately.** Since `RunCLIExitCode` now delegates to the dir-taking variant, every existing caller inherits the new semantics — truncated output plus `ErrWaitDelay` where they currently block indefinitely. That is strictly better behaviour (blocking forever on an already-killed process is never what a caller wants), which is precisely why it warrants its own change with an enumeration of every `RunCLIExitCode` caller and its own verification pass, rather than riding along on an unrelated phase while another agent is mid-rename in the same package.

Risk if left undone is bounded: it requires gt to fork a surviving child, which has not been observed, and the consequence is a slow ship rather than a wrong lane. The limitation is documented in a comment on `gtProbeTimeout` in `internal/cli/lane.go`, which names `WaitDelay` as the fix.

ops.text: Every existing caller of render.RunCLIExitCode and RunCLIExitCodeDir is enumerated, with the effect of truncated-output-plus-ErrWaitDelay assessed for each
WaitDelay is set on the dir-taking variant and a test proves a forking child cannot outlast the deadline
The deferral comment on gtProbeTimeout in internal/cli/lane.go is removed or updated once applied
